newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Italy to support Romania's NATO bid - official.
newsitem.headline: Italy to support Romania's NATO bid - official.

text.p: A senior Italian Foreign Ministry official said on Tuesday that Italy, which seeks a "special partnership" with Romania, will back the ex-communist country's efforts to gain quick admission to NATO.

Italian foreign affairs undersecretary Piero Fassino said that his country favoured a "simultaneous beginning of talks between NATO and all candidates" for the Alliance's first eastward expansion, to be announced at a July summit in Marid.

That approach "would avoid feelings of exclusion or frustration which might endanger the development of emerging democracies in eastern and Central Europe," he said after a meeting with Romania's centrist President Emil Constantinescu.
Romania is lobbying for support for first-wave admission to NATO, alongside more developed east Europeans Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic, viewed as near-certain entrants.

Constantinescu, whose centrists removed ex-communists from office in elections last November, is spearheading the drive to gain Western support for his country's foremost foreign policy goal of integration into NATO and the European Union.
"NATO's southern flank members have perfectly undersdtood the advantages of our country's geo-strategic position," he told reporters after talks with Fassino.

During a visit to Bucharest last month French President Jacques Chirac assured the new Romanian leaders of France's support for the ex-communist country's NATO membership bid, which he said would strengthen the southern flank of the Western defence alliance.
